draft.title: Amines and amides
card: an organic compound with a nitrogen atom bonded to carbon, as in the NH2 group of methylamine. The nitrogen has a lone pair of electrons.
the lone pair on nitrogen can accept a H+ ion from water. This makes an ammonium ion and OH- ions, but only a small fraction of amine molecules react, so amines are weak bases.
formed when a carboxylic acid joins an amine. The OH of the acid and an H from the amine leave as water, and the carbon and nitrogen bond together.
The amide link is a C=O group bonded directly to a nitrogen atom. It is called the amide linkage.
draft.remember: Amines have a nitrogen lone pair that accepts H+, so they are weak bases. An acid plus an amine makes an amide and water.

a.q: Why does methylamine act as a weak base in water?
opts: Its nitrogen lone pair accepts a H+ ion from water
Its nitrogen atom donates a H+ ion to water
Its carbon atoms accept a H+ ion from water
Its nitrogen releases OH- ions from its own structure
a.why: The lone pair on nitrogen accepts H+ from water, which leaves OH- ions in solution. Only a small fraction of molecules react, so the base is weak. Donating H+ would make it an acid, not a base.
a.clue: A base accepts H+. Which atom has a lone pair?

b.q: Ethanoic acid reacts with methylamine to form an organic product and water. Which statement about the organic product is correct?
opts: It is an amide with a C=O group bonded to nitrogen
It is an ester with a C=O group bonded to oxygen
It is an amine with no C=O group in its structure
It is an amide, and the water forms from the amine's N atom
b.why: A carboxylic acid joined to an amine makes an amide, with the C=O group bonded directly to nitrogen. An ester would form if the acid joined an alcohol, not an amine. The water comes from the OH of the acid and an H from the amine, not from the nitrogen atom.
b.clue: Which atom is bonded to the C=O carbon after the acid joins the amine?

a.best: Its nitrogen lone pair accepts a H+ ion from water

b.best: It is an amide with a C=O group bonded to nitrogen

check.summary: No problems found. The card is accurate at HSC level and both questions have a single clear answer.
